subject: Pilot economics: burn safeguard offer & pricing calibration
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thompson <claire@brightmart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot economics: burn safeguard offer & pricing calibration

Hi Claire — thanks again for a great call this morning. Quick recap of the numbers we discussed and a concrete proposal to keep your trial predictable while you ramp: 

Summary of customer targets (what I heard)
- Typical expected volume: 25–45M tokens / month for the initial 3-month pilot (peak ~60M in month 2)
- Budget band: $6k–$25k / month depending on usage banding and integration velocity
- Target economics you quoted: aim for ~$12 / 1M tokens as a long-term target to be comfortable with unit cost

Immediate ask from BrightMart
- Confirm the 25–45M tokens/month expected range and whether procurement needs a formal budget ceiling for the POC.

Redwood proposal (to keep pilot predictable)
- Pilot credit: we can grant a one-time $20,000 free-credit allowance for the 3-month pilot, applied pro-rata across months unless you prefer front-loading.
- Burn safeguard: if weekly burn rate exceeds the agreed threshold (we propose $9,000/week during peak month), we will temporarily throttle non-essential background requests and open a 24h ops window to triage usage patterns — this prevents surprising overages while keeping the app online.
- Unit price calibration: based on your volume band above, we can commit to an indicative unit of $11–$13 / 1M tokens for the pilot period (finalized in SOW).

Attachments: pilot_econ_model.xlsx (simple banded cost model) and a short_sow_draft.pdf that maps billing windows and the credit application.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the expected token range and whether procurement needs a PO or just a SOW?
2) If yes, I’ll send a short SOW + DocuSign link with the $20k credit and the guardrail language for review.
3) If you want a tighter burn threshold, tell me the weekly cap you prefer and we’ll adjust the SOW.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if that helps.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot_econ_model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 180KB)]
[Attachment: short_sow_draft.pdf (pdf, 45KB)]

From: Claire Thompson <claire@brightmart.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightMart Procurement <procurement@brightmart.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T08:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics: burn safeguard offer & pricing calibration

Rishi — thanks for the clear write-up. Quick answers: 
- Volume: we stand by the 25–45M tokens/mo expectation; product is comfortable with the peak scenario you noted (60M) if we can trust guardrails.
- Procurement: they will need an SOW + statement of work + budget ceiling to approve any credits. They typically ask for the maximum monthly liability (we’ll give you a number once we see the SOW).

$20k one-time credit sounds reasonable on the surface. Two requests before we sign: 
1) Can the burn safeguard include an automated email to our engineering lead when the weekly threshold triggers? (yes/no)
2) Can the pilot unit price be fixed for the pilot term (not subject to mid-pilot adjustments) — we prefer certainty for procurement.

If you can incorporate those items into the SOW, procurement will fast-track. I’ll loop them in once we have a DocuSign link.

—Claire
Head of Product, BrightMart
[File: procurement_contact.vcf]

Looping internal approvals/questions (Ben here, pricing ops):
- $20k one-time credit is within our discretionary range for named accounts; sign-off contingent on SOW language that:
  * defines application window (3 months)
  * states credits apply before invoicing consumption (i.e., credits consumed first)
  * includes explicit weekly threshold and what "throttle non-essential background requests" means (we should avoid hard cutoffs that break prod).
- Pricing fix: we can lock $12 / 1M tokens for pilot if BrightMart signs the SOW and agrees to a usage notification cadence (weekly) — that meets Claire’s procurement ask.

Operational suggestions:
- Include automated webhook to brightmart-eng@brightmart.com that posts weekly burn snapshots and a single alert at 80% of the weekly cap.
- Add an ops-on-call contact window (24h) to triage spikes; Redwood will not invoice for usage covered by credits.

If you want, Marissa can prepare the final SOW template with the guardrail language.

Ben
Director, Pricing & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final SOW + guardrail offer (DocuSign link) — action requested

Claire / Procurement — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is the short SOW I mentioned (summary below) and a DocuSign link to sign when you’re ready. Marissa has templated the guardrail language per Ben’s notes. 

Quick summary (what’s in the SOW)
- Pilot term: 90 days from Go-Live date
- One-time Redwood credit: $20,000 applied up-front to consumption; credits consumed before any invoiced usage
- Guaranteed pilot unit price: $12 / 1M tokens for the 90-day term (not renegotiated mid-term)
- Burn safeguard: weekly cap of $9,000 triggers (1) automated email to brightmart-eng@brightmart.com, (2) webhook payload to your status endpoint, and (3) a 24h ops window where Redwood will work with BrightMart to triage and, if necessary, apply soft-throttles to background requests. No hard service cut.
- Deliverables: pilot_econ_model.xlsx appended; short operational runbook in annex A.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/nd/xyz/brightmart-sow
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/319

Ask: procurement — if you can sign the SOW today or grant provisional approval, we’ll apply the $20k credit to your account immediately. Otherwise tell us the procurement PO/ceiling and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-minute call to walk procurement through the SOW terms.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
